articles.headline: U.S. Imposes New Iran-Related Sanctions, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026. These actions are part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting networks that generate revenue for Tehran's military, weapons, and nuclear programs.

The sanctions target five individuals, four entities, and nine vessels, including a Panama- and Greece-based law firm, Karnakis and Karnakis, accused of establishing shipping companies to transport Iranian steel, petroleum, and petrochemical products. Singapore-based Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd. and Dubai-based Whales Shipping Line LLC were also designated for providing services supporting Iranian oil and petrochemical shipments.

Additionally, OFAC announced the removal of certain Belarus and North Korea designations. The agency also issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance on these actions.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements Protecting American Intellectual Property Act Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026. This action aims to combat the theft of American intellectual property and protect U.S. economic interests.

Alongside these designations, OFAC issued associated General Licenses to provide guidance and authorize certain transactions related to the newly imposed sanctions. The specifics of the designated individuals or entities were not immediately detailed in the initial announcement.

These PAIPA designations underscore the U.S. government's commitment to leveraging sanctions authorities to address intellectual property theft, a critical concern for American innovation and competitiveness.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question on October 16, 2026. This update provides further clarity and potentially adjusts the scope of authorized activities concerning Venezuela.
The amendment follows recent developments in U.S.-Venezuela relations, including the removal of sanctions on a prominent Venezuelan official earlier in the week.
Such adjustments to General Licenses and FAQs are common as OFAC adapts its sanctions programs to evolving policy objectives and on-the-ground realities.

articles.headline: U.S. Designates Iranian Entities and Cuban Bank, Issues New General Licenses
body: The U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation on October 15, 2026.

The Cuba designation targeted Banco Internacional de Comercio, S.A. (BICSA) pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14404, which aims to pressure Cuba's government. This action is part of the Trump administration's intensified pressure campaign against Cuba, which has been criticized for exacerbating economic hardship on the island.
In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions to provide guidance on authorized transactions and compliance requirements.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan National Assembly Head from Sanctions List
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of Jorge Rodriguez, the head of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list on October 14, 2026.

This delisting follows a significant shift in U.S.-Venezuela relations, including major U.S.-Venezuela energy pacts and ongoing diplomatic talks. Rodriguez, who has led Venezuela's legislature since 2021, is the brother of interim President Delcy Rodriguez, who also had sanctions lifted earlier this year.

The move comes as Washington and Caracas pursue closer economic ties, with an arrangement granting the United States access to Venezuelan oilfields and foreign energy companies considering expanding operations in the country.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations on October 13, 2026. These designations target individuals and entities involved in illicit drug trafficking and terrorist financing activities globally.
These actions are part of ongoing efforts by the U.S. government to disrupt and dismantle criminal and terrorist networks that pose a threat to national security and international stability.

The specific details of the designated parties and the nature of their illicit activities were not immediately released in the initial announcement, but such designations typically result in the blocking of assets and prohibitions on transactions with U.S. persons.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a new Russia-related General License on October 9, 2026. This license, designated as Russia-related General License 131K, authorizes certain transactions for the negotiation of and entry into contingent contracts for the sale of Lukoil International GmbH and related maintenance activities.
This action suggests a targeted approach to managing the impact of sanctions on specific Russian entities, potentially to facilitate divestment or other limited engagements.
The issuance of General Licenses provides clarity and specific authorizations for activities that would otherwise be prohibited under existing sanctions regimes.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Amends Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 8, 2026, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting Iran's shadow fleet network.
In addition to the Iran-related actions, OFAC issued an Iran-related General License and an amended Russia-related General License.
These actions reflect the U.S. government's ongoing efforts to counter illicit activities by Iran and to adjust its sanctions framework concerning Russia.

articles.headline: Bank of America Fined $11,662,930 in OFAC Settlement
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to a settlement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for $11,662,930. This settlement addresses apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs, including those related to Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

This penalty is part of a broader enforcement action by the U.S. Treasury, which also included a $1.2 billion penalty from FinCEN and a $750 million civil money penalty from the OCC for BSA/AML deficiencies.

The settlement underscores the critical importance for financial institutions to maintain robust compliance programs to prevent sanctions violations and mitigate illicit finance risks across their operations.

The conflict has contributed to increased volatility in energy markets, with Brent crude forecast to average a little over US$100/barrel in the final quarter of 2026. The situation highlights the geopolitical sensitivities influencing global energy supplies and prices, underscoring the need for diversified energy strategies and diplomatic resolutions to regional conflicts.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
